author: reek
body: A binding made in a `trying` body does not escape that body: not into `falling back to`, not into `on failure`, and not past the `end`. Each of the three regions is its own lexical scope over the scope the try was written in.

author: reek
body: The decision this file records, because 2.23 asked for one. A fallback runs precisely when the body did NOT finish, so a body binding is, by construction, possibly-unwritten when the fallback reads it -- and the body re-runs from the top on every attempt, so even "the value" is not one value but one per attempt. Offering the fallback a name whose slot holds a partial attempt is offering it uninitialized memory with a friendly name on it. The three regions therefore do not share bindings.

author: reek
body: Nothing in the tree relied on the old behaviour: `trying` occurs in exactly one other source file (`try-smoke`), and no fallback there names anything from its body.

author: reek
body: The direction that made this visible is a MISCOMPILE, not a rejection, and the two halves disagreeing is what produced it. The type checker was already right -- `infer-act` is handed the untouched `env` for each region, so the fallback's `label` types as the global `Text`. The name resolver and the emitter were not: `Scope` is a `mutable` record and `scope-add-local` stores in place, so the body's `label` stayed resolvable; the emitter's locals are a flat prefix list that nothing popped, so `lookup-local` found the body's Integer slot. The checker said Text, the emitter loaded an Integer, and the concatenation below read that integer as a Text pointer.
